chunks: Hammad, from Hariz, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi 'Abd Allah, from Abi 'Abd Allah عليه السلام, who said:

A man from the Ansar, among the companions of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله, died. So the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله went out in his funeral procession, walking. Then some of his companions said to him, “Will you not ride, O Messenger of Allah?” He said, “Indeed, I dislike to ride while the angels are walking.”

Al-Shaykh, may Allah Most High support him, said: When the salat over him has been completed, his bier should be brought near to his grave and placed upon the ground, and one should pause over him for a little while. Then he should be moved forward a little, then one should pause over him for a little while, then he should be brought to the edge of the grave. His head should be placed toward that side which corresponds to the place of his feet in his grave. His guardian should descend into the grave, or whoever the guardian instructs to do so. He should tuck up his garment when descending and loosen his buttons, and if another descends with him to assist him, that is permissible.

key_terms.الصَّلَاةِ: the funeral salat performed over the deceased
key_terms.الْمَلَائِكَةُ: the angels, whose presence signifies honor and solemnity at the funeral
key_terms.شَفِيرِ الْقَبْرِ: the edge or lip of the grave
key_terms.لِمَعُونَتِهِ: for assisting him in the burial
key_terms.وَلِيُّهُ: his guardian or the one with authority over his burial arrangements

ai.seo_question: What does this hadith teach about funeral procession etiquette and the proper way to bring a deceased person to the grave?
ai.summary: This report describes the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله walking in a funeral procession out of reverence, saying that he disliked riding while the angels were walking. It also records juridical instructions about how the deceased should be brought to the grave, paused with gradually, and lowered into the grave by the guardian or his appointed representative.
